title: The direction budget this run was given is not the direction budget it used
detects: An artefact whose direction ceiling and applied direction count disagree. `max_directions` is what the search was allowed to use and `num_directions` is what the saved model actually had removed, and the search picks its budget inside the ceiling, so the two come apart routinely. An arm named after its ceiling is named after a setting it did not apply, and two such arms compared as a budget comparison are two searches wearing the labels of an experiment nobody ran.
incident: Ours, 2026-08-03. A five-seed comparison of a one-direction arm against a three-direction arm finished with complete separation at p equals 0.004 and was withdrawn in full, because both arms had ablated one direction per layer. It compared two searches rather than two direction budgets, and its finding, that refusal in that model is one direction, was withdrawn with it. Nothing in either arm's artefact was false; the ceiling and the applied count were both recorded, and the comparison was built on the first.
remedy: Quote `num_directions` with `dir_mode`, which is what was applied, and treat `max_directions` as what it is: a ceiling on the search. If the arms of a comparison were meant to differ in direction budget, check that their applied counts actually differ before reporting anything; if they do not, the comparison did not run and re-labelling it will not make it a result.
false_positive: A ceiling above the applied count is the NORMAL outcome of a search that was free to use fewer directions, and on a single artefact quoted on its own it is not a defect at all. Medium confidence for exactly that reason: the finding is that this artefact cannot support a claim about its ceiling, which is only a problem when somebody makes one. It is genuinely noisy on any run with `--max-directions` above one, and the honest reading is that it tells a reader which number to quote rather than that something went wrong. It also reads ONE document, so it cannot see the case it was written for, which is two arms that agree when they were supposed to differ; the engine runs one artefact at a time.
